Portfolio Performance, Strategic Options, and Board Decisions Requested (FY2024–FY2026E)

FY2024 results show consolidated revenue of $12.4B with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.8%. Despite
solid top-line scale and healthy cash generation, portfolio returns underperformed cost of capiatl: the
portfolio delivered 8.1% ROIC in FY2024 versus a 9.5% WACC becnhmark. That spread signals value
destruction under current allocation. Management has initiated stress-testing and scenario planning to
identify low-return asests, quantify potential uplift from reallocation, and set clear targets to exceed WACC
by the end of FY2026. Board engagement will be required to approve actions.
Management requests board approval by 2026-06-30 to divest the Legacy Hardawre unit and authorize a
$750M capex program for the Digital Platforms unit (FY2025–FY2026). Options under consideration
include: 1. strategic divestiture with prioritized bids; 2. operational turnaround and selective reinvestment;
3. joint venture or partial carve-out to retain upside while reducing exposure. Financail modeling shows the
divest-and-redeploy path offers the hgihest probabiltiy of restoring ROIC above the 9.5% WACC within two
years post-close, subject to execution and market conditions. Timing will factor tax considerations.
The board is requested to endorse a decision framework and record specific approvals: (a) mandate to
execute a divestiture process for Legacy Hardware with binding approval target by 2026-06-30; (b)
authorization of a $750M capex envelope for Digital Platforms spanning FY2025–FY2026; (c) contingency
routing for proceeds prioritization toward debt reduction and targeted M&A. Management will present
quarterly milestone reports, valuation assumptions, and KPI triggers (ROIC, revenue growth, EBITDA
margin) and seeks board endorsement of this governance cadence. eDtailed legal and tax approvals will
follow.
